title: Two Sum
description:
Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to `target`.

Exactly one valid pair exists and you may not use the same element twice. Print the two indices `i j` with `i < j` (0-based).
inputFormat:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n space-separated integers
Line 3: target
outputFormat: Two integers i and j (i < j) separated by a space.

title: Valid Parentheses
description:
Given a string `s` containing only the characters `()[]{}`, decide whether it is valid.

A string is valid when every opening bracket is closed by the same type of bracket and brackets close in the correct order.
inputFormat: A single line containing s (no spaces).
outputFormat: `true` if the string is valid, otherwise `false`.

examples.explanation: Each bracket is closed in order.

title: Binary Search
description:
Given a sorted array of **distinct** integers and a `target`, print the index of `target` in the array, or `-1` if it is not present.

Your solution should run in O(log n) time per query.
inputFormat:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n sorted distinct integers
Line 3: target

title: Maximum Subarray
description: Given an integer array `nums`, find the contiguous subarray (containing at least one number) with the largest sum and print that sum.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description: Given a string `s`, print the length of the longest substring that contains no repeated characters.
inputFormat: A single line containing s (printable ASCII, no spaces).
outputFormat: The length of the longest substring without repeating characters.

title: Merge Intervals
description: Given `n` closed intervals `[l, r]`, merge all overlapping intervals (intervals that touch, like [1,4] and [4,5], also overlap) and print the result sorted by start.
inputFormat:
Line 1: n
Next n lines: l r
outputFormat:
Line 1: k, the number of merged intervals
Next k lines: l r of each merged interval in increasing order.

title: Number of Islands
description: Given an `R x C` grid of `'1'` (land) and `'0'` (water), count the islands. An island is a group of land cells connected horizontally or vertically.
inputFormat:
Line 1: R C
Next R lines: a string of C characters, each '0' or '1'

title: Coin Change
description: Given coin denominations and a target `amount`, print the minimum number of coins needed to make the amount (unlimited coins of each type). Print `-1` if the amount cannot be made.
inputFormat:
Line 1: n amount
Line 2: n coin values
outputFormat: The minimum number of coins, or -1.

examples.explanation: 3 cannot be made with coins of 2.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
description:
Given an integer array `nums`, print the length of the longest **strictly** increasing subsequence.

An O(n²) DP is a good start; aim for O(n log n) using patience sorting with binary search.
outputFormat: Length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

title: Shortest Paths (Dijkstra)
description: Given a directed graph with `n` nodes (1..n) and `m` weighted edges with non-negative weights, compute the shortest distance from source `s` to every node. Print `-1` for unreachable nodes.
inputFormat:
Line 1: n m
Next m lines: u v w (edge u → v with weight w)
Last line: s
outputFormat: n space-separated integers: the distance to nodes 1..n (or -1).

examples.explanation: 1→2→3 costs 3, cheaper than the direct edge of 5.
From node 2 nothing else is reachable.

title: Trapping Rain Water
description: Given `n` non-negative integers representing an elevation map where each bar has width 1, compute how much water can be trapped after raining.
inputFormat:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n non-negative integers (bar heights)
